answer: Verifiable delay functions curb Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve an unparallelizable sequential cipher. Because intermediate states remain opaque as onyx, attackers cannot shortcut steps, stranding botnets on a computational mesa where parallel threads yield no speedup. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of wall-clock time and dedicated electrical power per identity. A key limitation is that custom ASICs allow wealthy adversaries to compute steps faster than standard nodes.
